newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil, seeking savings, cuts federal benefits.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, seeking savings, cuts federal benefits.

text.p: The Brazilian government, seeking to keep a grip on public spending, introduced on Monday new rules that reduce a wide range of benefits enjoyed by the federal work force.

The new rules, published in the government's official gazette, went into effect immediately and were aimed at eliminating or reducing benefits considered to be overly generous, a spokesman for the Administration Ministry said.
"They are clearly measures that will cut spending a little bit, make civil servants do more work and help improve management of the public sector," the spokesman said.

For example, federal government employees will be entitled to only 60 days paid leave to take care of sick family members, down from 180 days. Workers seeking elected office may now only take three months off for campaigning, down from six months.

The newspaper Correio Braziliense said 31,000 civil servants took advantage of the benefit to run for office in last year's local elections. Also gone under the new rules are bonuses paid to employees working in remote areas of Brazil.

The government hopes its civil service reform bill, currently in Congress, will prove a powerful tool in reducing public sector spending on pay and pensions by federal, state and municipal authorities.
But delays in approving the bill have forced authorities to seek interim measures to control costs.
